decisions.quote:
The replication study reaffirmed some of Marvel's (2016) findings, while also yielding some different results.

APSB has a consistent negative effect on citizens' evaluations of public sector performance. However, contrary to

expectations, the influence of performance information on the performance evaluation is not as short-lived as Mar-

vel (2016) found. Under certain conditions, individuals' APSB could be altered by favorable performance information.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly frame their overall replication findings as mixed, confirming Marvel's (2016) findings on H1 (supported) and H2 (unsupported) regarding the negative effect of APSB on performance evaluations, while finding contrary results on H3 and H4 (both supported in Marvel 2016 but unsupported in the replication, as the positive effect of performance information lasted beyond 2 days and altered implicit attitudes under the classic IAT). Under the codebook rules, confirming the main bias effect in the abstract does not override explicit overall framing and tested hypothesis contrasts showing that some findings replicated and others did not.
